blueprint_refs: protocol: "Optionally, at each time_bin, compute co-location contacts among residents currently at each place."

evidence.metrics: No outputs/metrics for co-location; POI.current_occupancy never changes in simulation.

no-colocation-layer-implemented.error_identification: Blueprint requires/permits co-location contact and occupancy updates, but simulation generates only resident trajectories; occupancy/contact layer is absent, so any downstream social/contact analyses would be impossible.
no-colocation-layer-implemented.root_cause_analysis: MobilitySimulator.simulate_days appends Event objects but never increments/decrements POI.current_occupancy and never computes contact events; there is no time-bin loop or overlap logic.
no-colocation-layer-implemented.correct_approach: Add event windows by sampling dwell times (already sampled) and record (arrival, departure) per agent per POI. Update POI.current_occupancy on arrival/departure. If enabled, compute co-location contacts per time_bin (e.g., 10 minutes) by grouping agents present at each POI during each bin and emitting contact pairs; store separately from trajectories to avoid breaking output schema.
no-colocation-layer-implemented.key_insight: If blueprint defines an interaction layer (occupancy/contact), implement at least the state updates and a minimal event log; otherwise metrics and extensions tied to that layer cannot be validated.

blueprint_refs: execution: "Optimize calibratable parameters ... by minimizing validation loss"

evidence.metrics: Calibration objective reported as best_objective_on_training; validation metrics remain mediocre (topk_poi_recall≈0.184, stop_count_abs_mean_error≈1.59).

calibration-on-training-not-validation.error_identification: The system calibrates parameters against training days rather than the blueprint-specified validation loss, which risks overfitting and mis-calibration for held-out dates.
calibration-on-training-not-validation.root_cause_analysis: In main(), RandomSearchCalibrator.fit is called with train_ground_truth_by_agent=train_by_agent and train_dates_by_agent=train_dates; it does not use val_by_agent/val_dates for objective scoring.
calibration-on-training-not-validation.correct_approach: Change calibrator.fit signature/usage to accept validation_ground_truth_by_agent and validation_dates_by_agent (from holdout_split). Use training only for fitting global/agent models; run simulation over validation dates for scoring. If compute cost is a concern, calibrate on a subset of validation dates and then evaluate on full validation.
calibration-on-training-not-validation.key_insight: Separate 'fit models' (training) from 'tune parameters' (validation); otherwise calibration optimizes the wrong target and validation metrics won’t reflect intended objective.

stop-count-distribution-mismatch-and-ear.error_identification: Simulated days have notably different numbers of stops than validation (average error ~1.6 stops/day; KL divergence ~0.50).
stop-count-distribution-mismatch-and-ear.root_cause_analysis: simulate_days samples n_stops but then applies an independent end-day hazard at every step, effectively shrinking the realized stop count below the sampled target. The hazard is not conditioned on remaining planned stops or time budget; it can double-count “end day” mechanisms.
stop-count-distribution-mismatch-and-ear.correct_approach: Make stop count coherent with ending: either (a) remove hazard and force exactly n_stops (except when time runs out), or (b) treat n_stops as a prior and use hazard to generate the stop count directly (stop when hazard triggers), not both. If keeping both, gate hazard so it only applies after reaching at least a minimum fraction of n_stops or after a late-day threshold.
stop-count-distribution-mismatch-and-ear.key_insight: Don’t sample a target count and also apply an unconditional stopping hazard; align the generative story so one mechanism determines stop count.

evidence.metrics: topk_poi_recall≈0.184 on validation; calibrated softmax_temperature≈4.99 (near max) and candidate_set_topk_from_transition_graph=180 (very large).

poi-choice-too-random-high-temperature-a.error_identification: The simulator fails to reproduce agents’ commonly visited POIs (recall@10 ~0.18), while calibrated parameters indicate near-uniform sampling pressure.
poi-choice-too-random-high-temperature-a.root_cause_analysis: With high softmax_temperature, utility differences from affinity/popularity/distance have limited effect, and _candidate_pois adds many random POIs (up to ~50 extras) after including up to topk transition neighbors, increasing exploration. This combination dilutes selection of anchor POIs, hurting top-k recall.
poi-choice-too-random-high-temperature-a.correct_approach: Constrain calibration/search to avoid degenerate high-temperature solutions (e.g., use log-uniform prior favoring lower temperatures, or cap temperature to ~2 unless justified). Reduce random extra candidates or weight candidates (e.g., sample extras proportional to popularity/affinity rather than uniform). Add a recency/anchor bonus: explicitly include agent’s top-N affinity POIs in candidate list for matching recall metric.
poi-choice-too-random-high-temperature-a.key_insight: If a metric rewards repeating known locations, avoid parameter regimes that make choice close to uniform; candidate generation and temperature jointly control memorization vs exploration.

blueprint_refs: exogenous_signals.travel_cost_distance: "distance-based penalty ... penalty strength is calibratable"

evidence.metrics: trip_distance_wasserstein≈1.10 km; w_distance_decay is applied as u -= w * dist (linear).

distance-penalty-linear-in-km-dominates-.error_identification: Trip distance distribution remains meaningfully different from validation (Wasserstein ~1.1 km), suggesting the distance model is not matching empirical decay.
distance-penalty-linear-in-km-dominates-.root_cause_analysis: Blueprint implies a distance-decay utility term; current implementation uses a linear penalty in raw km. Many mobility models use log-distance, power-law, or exponential decay; linear km can be too strong at long distances and too weak at short distances depending on scale, and it ignores agent-specific mobility_radius_preference_km.
distance-penalty-linear-in-km-dominates-.correct_approach: Replace linear penalty with a calibrated decay form consistent with training: e.g., u -= w * (dist / (profile.mobility_radius_preference_km+eps)) or u -= w * log(1+dist). Optionally fit a global/agent radius parameter from training (already computed) and use it in utility.
distance-penalty-linear-in-km-dominates-.key_insight: Distance features should be scale-normalized (global or per-agent) and use a decay form that matches empirical distance distributions; raw linear km is rarely robust.

blueprint_refs: action_decision_policy: "next event time = current_time + travel_time(distance) + dwell_time"

evidence.metrics: Calibration drives travel_time_speed_kmph high (~70.6 km/h), suggesting timing components may be mis-attributed.

dwell-time-estimated-from-inter-event-ga.error_identification: Timing model likely mis-specified: dwell-time distribution is learned from raw time gaps between consecutive events, but simulation adds both travel time and dwell time, risking double-counting and forcing calibration to compensate (e.g., unrealistically high speed).
dwell-time-estimated-from-inter-event-ga.root_cause_analysis: In estimate_models_from_training(), dwell_gap_by_category uses gap = nxt.time - cur.time directly as a dwell sample. In simulation, inter-event gap becomes travel_time(distance)+dwell_time, so learned dwell already includes travel, biasing dwell upward and distorting travel speed calibration.
dwell-time-estimated-from-inter-event-ga.correct_approach: When fitting dwell parameters, subtract an estimated travel time component from gaps (using an initial speed guess or distances where available). Alternatively, fit a joint model: treat observed gap as dwell+travel and estimate dwell parameters by regressing out travel distance or using EM-like updates during calibration.
dwell-time-estimated-from-inter-event-ga.key_insight: If training provides only timestamps, inter-event gaps are composites; don’t reuse them as dwell directly if the simulator separately models travel time.

transition-model-ignores-poi-level-perso.error_identification: Category transitions and POI recall are underperforming, consistent with missing personalization at the POI transition level.
transition-model-ignores-poi-level-perso.root_cause_analysis: The simulator computes personal transitions only for coarse categories. POI choice uses global POI transition graph probabilities (trans_probs derived from global edge counts) and agent POI affinities, but no agent-specific POI->POI transition prior is learned/applied.
transition-model-ignores-poi-level-perso.correct_approach: During training, compute per-agent POI transition counts (poi_i->poi_{i+1}) and normalize. In _choose_poi, add a personal transition term (weighted) alongside global transition term. Also use the global transition graph to form candidate sets, but score with a mixture of personal/global POI transitions.
transition-model-ignores-poi-level-perso.key_insight: If evaluation rewards reproducing habitual sequences, personalization must apply to transitions, not just marginal POI frequencies.

evidence.metrics: Stop-count KL may be unstable if distributions have disjoint supports; implementation smooths only over observed support.

stop-count-distribution-smoothing-suppor.error_identification: Stop-count KL can be biased/high because smoothing is applied only to keys present in each distribution, not over the union support with a shared prior.
stop-count-distribution-smoothing-suppor.root_cause_analysis: _stop_count_dist builds support = sorted(ctr.keys()) and applies smoothing only on that support. When later aligning supports in compute_metrics, missing keys get EPS+1e-9, but not the same smoothing mass as present keys.
stop-count-distribution-smoothing-suppor.correct_approach: Compute smoothed distributions over the union support directly (in compute_metrics): for each k in union, use count(k)+alpha, then normalize. This yields symmetric smoothing consistent with the metric definition.
stop-count-distribution-smoothing-suppor.key_insight: When comparing discrete distributions, apply smoothing on a common support; per-distribution supports create artifacts that inflate divergence.

blueprint_refs: scale_granularity.time_step: "Seconds are retained in parsing but rounded for simulation."

evidence.metrics: Time parsing drops seconds entirely; could slightly affect time-of-day histograms.

missing-event-driven-minute-rounding-sec.error_identification: Parser ignores seconds rather than retaining then rounding, deviating from blueprint (minor but can add noise to minute histograms if seconds carry structure).
missing-event-driven-minute-rounding-sec.root_cause_analysis: parse_hhmmss_to_minute_of_day parses HH and MM only; seconds are discarded even when provided.
missing-event-driven-minute-rounding-sec.correct_approach: Parse optional seconds; convert to minute with rounding (e.g., minute = hh*60+mm + (ss>=30)). Clamp to [0,1439]. Keep robust stripping logic.
missing-event-driven-minute-rounding-sec.key_insight: Time discretization should be explicit and consistent with spec; even small rounding rules can systematically shift histogram-based metrics.
